preview: An interview experience detailing the 2022 Summer Internship process at JP Morgan Chase & Co., including an online coding round, Hirevue video interview, and the Code for Good hackathon.
content: JP Morgan Chase & Co. Interview Experience Sarah Tisekar | T.Y.B.Tech Computer Engineering 2019-23 For 2022 Summer Internship(On-campus) 28th December 2021 JP Morgan Chase & Co. was the first company to visit our campus for Internships for 3rd Year students. A total of 130 students applied for this. Eligibility: ● Degree – B.Tech / BE / MCA ● Streams / Specialization – Computer Science, Information Science/ Information Technology, Electronics, Electrical, Electronics & Telecommunications ● Backlogs – No current backlogs ● A well-rounded academic background with a minimum aggregate of 7 CGPA until date. Software Engineer Program Roadshow flagship event (2nd Feb 2021) This is a one-stop opportunity for you to know more about JP Morgan Chase & Co. and the significant impact that technology has on their businesses. You will hear from JPMC leaders and learn about their work and culture. You will get acquainted with their Campus Hiring programs, learn about the application and shortlisting process for the Software Engineer Program, and understand how you stand a chance to join their firm as Interns. This is a great opportunity for you to find out how they build diverse and inclusive teams, and how you can build a career with JPMC. Online Coding Round (20th Feb 2021, 6 PM IST) ● An online test was conducted on HackerRank. ● The test duration was 75 minutes. ● It was a coding test of 100 marks having 2 programming questions, each of 50 marks. It was mandatory to attempt both the questions. Online Video interview (12th March 2021) The Online Video Interview was conducted on Hirevue. We had the opportunity to try practice questions before the interview began. Once ready, HireVue will then ask questions, which we’ll record our responses to via video. We were asked two questions. The questions were typically what you would expect during an HR interview round. I don’t have a very clear recollection of the questions. But I guess the first question was along the lines “mention a time in your life when you made a mistake at work or school" and the second was “describe a time in your life when you did something overwhelming or overambitious”. The answer to each question was not supposed to exceed two minutes. We had one opportunity to re-record each response if desired. If we chose to re-record a response, the updated response would automatically be submitted as final. The deadline for completing the video interview was 14th March 2021. Tips for the video interview? 1. Prepare! You have Tips for Success and resources to guide you. 2. Find a time and place which ensures a quiet, distraction-free environment with good lighting. 3. Dress professionally and make sure the camera and sound on your computer or mobile device are working. 4. Make sure to try the practice questions before your interview begins. Based on the performance in the coding test and the video interview, 18 students were shortlisted for the final Code For Good event. CFG Bootcamp Ahead of the 2021 Code for Good Hackathon, a series of optional workshops and Q&A sessions were conducted to help us settle into a collaborative virtual environment and prepare for the big event. The CFG Bootcamp was designed to introduce us to key tools and platforms that would assist us in having a successful hack over the event weekend, especially for someone new to the hackathon space. Line-up of sessions: ● Introduction to Git (29th June 2021, 5 pm) A walkthrough of the fundamental concepts and commands in Git to help prep for a collaborative coding environment. ● The Art of Powerful Questions (1st July 2021, 5:30 pm) To learn all about how Powerful Questions helps to build better relationships with clients and create more inclusive designs by encouraging a mode of inquiry, varied perspectives, and co-creating solutions. ● Git Q&A ( 2nd July 2021, 5:00 pm) Now that we had learned the 101s of Git and had the chance to try it out, we had a session lined up where we could engage with JPMC’s subject matter experts on Git to clear any doubts/questions that we had. ● Code for Good Event Q&A (6th July 2021, 5:00 pm) A 1.5-hour session focused on reviewing the hackathon event structure and the Code for Good virtual platform set-up. We could seek any clarifications we needed regarding the hackathon format. Code for Good ( 8th - 11th July 2021 ) JP Morgan’s annual coding challenge – “Code For Good” - is dedicated towards solving real-world problems for nonprofits. The Code For Good is also a hiring event and the only means by which we could apply for Internship opportunities under the “Software Engineer Program (SEP) 2022” at JP Morgan. The Code for Good challenge gives you the chance to put your coding skills to work helping nonprofits. It’s also a great opportunity to see whether a career in financial services technology is for you. Over the course of a weekend, you’ll work with a team to develop a technology solution for a leading nonprofit. You’ll work alongside JPMorgan Chase technologists, learning from their experience as you creatively solve real-world problems faced by social organizations. This is a great way to put your creative ideas into practice to help those who need them most. About the event: Teams of five to seven (5-7) students will compete against each other on behalf of a charity assigned to them in order to provide a technological solution to a problem that the charity faces. The team or teams which, in the opinion of J.P. Morgan Services India Private Limited (“JPMC”), make the best attempt at developing such a solution will receive a prize for themselves. Based on their performance during the Code For Good, students that truly stand out as exceptional will get an offer to join the Firm for the Software Engineering Program Internship. There were a total of 95 teams this year. Platforms Used: The organizers had provided every team with a private GitHub repository. A Code For Good slack workspace was also created for announcements and activities that were to be conducted. The Hackathon was conducted on the BeMyApp platform. All teams were given unique Zoom links for discussions throughout the hackathon. Here is a detailed breakdown of the Hackathon: Student Networking (8th July 2021, 5:30 PM) Since the teams were formed by the CFG organizers, it was very likely to find team members from different Colleges and even different states within India. This necessitated the need for a student networking period wherein we could get to know each other better, understand the strengths and weaknesses of our team, discuss the tech stack everyone was familiar with and strategize for the hack. To help us bond better, each team was given a unique zoom link. There were several activities we were asked to do as a team. We had an Icebreaker round wherein we had to find out our common interests as a team, favorite meme/GIF, favorite framework to work with, the trickiest framework to work with, and so on. We also had many activities to do some of which included using a meme to best describe our team and post it on the #TeamMeme slack channel. The meme we chose to describe us was the “perfectly balanced” one. The reason for choosing this meme? Well, we had decided to make both a Web and Mobile Application. So we had three members who were familiar with React (who would make the Frontend for the Web App), two who were proficient with Nodejs and APIs, etc.(who would do the Backend), and two of us who would make the Mobile App in Flutter. Also, a few of us had worked previously with AI/ML. Hence we thought we were a perfect balance as we had a decent mix of tech stacks. Hackathon Survival Guide (8th July 2021, 6:30 PM) This was basically a speaker session wherein we were given a lot of advice and many tips and tricks to surviving the hack. While there were so many things to take away from this session, a few have been summarized here: ● Brainstorm ○ Think out of the box. ○ What unique touch are you going to provide? ○ Evaluate each idea. ○ Discuss, talk and set targets. ○ Be realistic. ● Organize your Team Decide high-level roles and responsibilities ○ Pick a leader - to speak on behalf of the team, settle disputes, remove roadblocks, and set directions. ○ Pick a timekeeper - that will keep you on task and schedule. ○ Regroup and do it often. Quick cycle time is an important advantage. ○ One person can serve in multiple roles. ○ You should change roles as needed. ● Use tools ○ These will save you time ○ Save time getting project structure and build files created. ○ Using tools like Spring Initializer and Create React App help set up projects and initial dependencies. ○ Most of these resources are CLI tools or web GUIs that create the project’s structure, define its required dependencies files(pom.xml, package.json, etc.), and set up a few simple run scripts. ● Scientific Method to the rescue! ○ Reach out to SME/ Team mentors, leverage the resources available to you. ○ Understand the situation ■ Got an error? What does it say? ○ Identify the root cause of the problem ■ Changed something recently? Revert!? ○ Develop an effective action plan ■ Got an idea? Decide how you are going to test it! ○ Execute and modify, until the problem is solved. ■ Run your test, evaluate the result, modify as needed, test again. Hackathon Tool Prep (8th July 2021, 7:45 PM) This was Another Speaker session by an Ex-CFG participant. This session was focused on how to improve productivity and how to use project management tools like Trello, Github Projects, etc. during the hackathon. Our team decided to go ahead with Trello. So we created a workspace in Trello. We created 3 boards one each for Web Frontend, Backend, and the Mobile App. We then made a list of things to be done and categorized them into three lists called On-Going, Completed, and Ambition(for extra things that we would do only after completing the bare requirements) for each board. After the events scheduled for the day were over, we decide to join our team zoom meet again and discuss and strategize a few more things. After which everyone went off to learn things from the resource pool that we had collected. 9th July 2021 There were a lot of events scheduled on this day, like the Opening Ceremony, FLARE Workshop, a session on Power of Empathy in Coding but we didn’t much attention to those sessions as we were engrossed in discussions for the Hack. We decided on going through problem statements of previous year's CFG and see how we as a team would come up with solutions for the same, what all features would we include, and were we able to think of something out of the box. Mentor - Team Huddle (9th July 2021, 7 PM) This was the most awaited of all the events. Do remember that the mentors play a very important role in you getting the internship at JPMC. The Mentor - Team Huddle was where the mentors would get the first impression of each one of us. At JPMC, there is no hierarchy and no one is considered superior or inferior to another. Hence we were expected to address everyone by their first name. It did feel very awkward at first to address our mentors by their first name rather than calling them Sir or Ma’am. But eventually, we got slightly accustomed to it. Just like we had an Icebreaker and Activities lined up for us during the Student Networking event, we had them for the Mentor - Team Huddle as well. The Mentors were very kind and supportive and there was a lot to learn from them and their experiences. It was a lot of fun carrying out these activities with our Mentors. We really needed that time off the pressure and stress of the Hackathon that was to start the next day. Challenges go Live! (10th July 2021, 7:00 AM) At 7:00 AM the Problem Statements were live on the CFG platform. There were around 11 Non-Profit Organizations each with a problem statement. Each Problem Statement consisted of a Mission, Context, Challenge, Additional Considerations, and Technology Baseline. We had one hour to read through the challenges and decide which one we wanted to go ahead with. Challenge Presentation(10th July 2021, 8:00 AM) Each Organization presented its problem statement and elaborated a little more on what type of a solution they were expecting from us. As the Organizations were presenting, we were simultaneously discussing our preferences. At 9:00 AM, the preferences form was rolled out, and we had to fill them ASAP as the Challenges would be allotted on a first-come-first-serve basis. Each Organization was allotted only to the first 5 teams that chose it as their first preference. Team Challenge Alignments (10th July 2021, 9:30 AM) The final allotments were out, unfortunately, we didn’t get our first preference but we were glad we at least got our second preference. Q&A with the Social Good Organization(10th July 2021, 10:15 AM) This was a Q&A session wherein we could clear our doubts regarding the problem statements with the Organization we had been allotted. This was our chance to get to know what exactly the Organization wanted us to come up with, as we found the problem statements pretty vague. The more questions we would ask the more details we would get, thereby giving us a clear idea of what we wanted to implement and what features would be crucial for the solution. However, we didn’t want to waste any time as the hackathon had started. So we decided to split up, two of us stayed back in the zoom meet to attend the Q&A and gather as much information as we could while the rest started coding the basic features of the App that we had discussed earlier. After the Q&A session, we joined the rest and explained all the requirements of the Organization that were expected to be in our solution. We then split up into breakout rooms. We had three breakout rooms one for the Web Frontend, one for the Backend, and one for the Mobile App. The mentors were also there in our team zoom meet. They were carefully listening to our conversations, giving us feedback and suggestions from time to time. We did have frequent group discussions to check on everyone's progress. We also occasionally moved between breakout rooms to help with errors, API failures, App crashes, etc. We also leveraged the help of SME’s whenever we were stuck. Everyone was so engrossed in coding that the Mentors literally had to tell us to take a break XD. Submission Requirements (10th July 2021, 9 PM) Just like the Q&A session, to save time only two of our team members joined the meet where they explained the submission requirements while the rest of us continued to code. We were supposed to submit our project on the BeMyApp platform. All instructions on how to submit the project were given during this session. The two team members noted down all the things that would be required for submission. Some of which included the GitHub repository link, screenshots of the App, project description which should include how our solution solves the challenge presented to us, drive link of the video demonstration, etc. The two of them joined us again after the session was over. And the coding continued. The Mentors were there in the meet for a significant amount of time. They kept motivating us. They also spoke to us on topics other than the hack like what our future plans were and the like. They also lightened the tense environment by occasionally cracking jokes and taking team pictures. The mentors wished us luck and left the zoom meet at around 12 AM. We continued coding even in the wee hours. Some of the team members decided to take a small break while the rest of us continued coding, knowing very clearly that we wouldn’t be able to rest for even a second until the App was complete. The CFG organizers had also arranged fun games and activities during the event and participants were encouraged to take part in them whenever they felt like taking a break. But no one from our group took part in any of them XD. Coding Cut-off (11th July 2021, 10 AM) We had to stop coding, and could not commit anything to our Github repository after this. The Mentors joined us again to see our completed project. We now had one hour to submit our solutions. We had the option to do a live demo or a pre-recorded video presentation for the technical judging round that was scheduled at 11:30 AM. We didn’t want to risk a live demo and hence we decided to go forward with the pre-recording option. It was at this moment that we realized that the Web App was suddenly not working :( We began to panic a little but the Mentors told us to record the Mobile App that was working and to focus on the pitch, as pitching the solution was very important. They told us that not all the people judging from the Non - profit Organizations have a technical background and hence pitching to them about how our solution solves their challenges was essential to ace the round. Since we were using Flutter, we decided to tell the judges that it can be used as a Web App as well as a Mobile App. We didn’t lose hope and began to record our presentation. Since we were short on time, we reckoned that if everyone spoke about a portion of the App, It would take a long time. So it was decided that I would do the presentation and speak about our solution approach, all the features of the App, and how it solves all the challenges presented in the problem statement. We did have many bloopers in the process while recording XD. We finished recording exactly 1 minute before the deadline. We immediately uploaded it to the drive, added the link to the BeMyApp platform, and were able to submit our project just in time. Technical Judging (11th July 2021, 11:30 AM) We presented our solution to the social good organization that had been allotted to us. The judges complimented our Apps UI and were impressed with the algorithm that we used to match the posts/openings to volunteers and NGOs based on their interests. They then proceeded to ask us a few questions and we were able to answer them. After looking at the solutions of other teams, we were mind-blown with the level of innovation and creativity they had used in their solutions. We knew for sure that we didn’t stand a chance to qualify for the next round. Unfortunately, but not surprisingly, we didn’t make it to the next round. But we were glad that we did our best. It was a complete roller coaster ride filled with ups and downs. There was a lot to learn from each and every person that I interacted with during the hackathon. It was definitely the experience of a lifetime. Event Shortlists: Roughly less than a month after CFG, the list of students selected for the Internship was out. 13 students were selected from our college, and surprisingly I was one of them. I was elated to find out that most of my teammates were selected for the Internship.
